title: BrickWright: Agentic Creation of Physically Feasible Brick Builds
title_zh: BrickWright：用于物理可行积木构建的智能体化创作

paragraphs.en: Frontier coding agents are becoming increasingly adept at 3D modeling. Yet, they still face challenges when building objects meant to be assembled in the physical world, often creating invalid assemblies with floating, colliding, or disconnected parts. We argue that providing agents with tools for assembling builds and verifying their physical feasibility is sufficient for them to produce physically valid assemblies that still adhere to input prompts. Focusing on the domain of LEGO ® brick builds, we present BrickWright, a framework for generating physically feasible brick builds from text or image prompts using pre-trained agents, where a build is physically feasible if it uses only real parts, has no colliding or floating parts, and forms a connected structure if possible. BrickWright guides agents to create builds by writing code with BrickLayer, a Python toolkit with two main components: an ergonomic brick assembly API that halves inference cost compared to working in raw LDraw, and a validator that provides feedback on physical feasibility. Whereas baseline agents achieve physical validity rates ranging from only 9% (GPT-6 Luna) to 69% (GPT-6 Astra), BrickWright-guided agents achieve 100% validity on a sample of 512 prompts, while improving prompt adherence for lightweight agents and maintaining it for stronger agents. Additionally, they outperform specialized models on the text-to-brick task. Code is available on our project page: avalovelace1.github.io/brickwright .

paragraphs.en: Large language model (LLM) agents are becoming increasingly adept at 3D modeling. Without additional fine-tuning, commercially available agents can successfully produce articulated objects [ 58 , 45 ] , scenes [ 52 ] , and constructive solid geometry models [ 27 ] . However, they still face challenges when building objects for the physical world. We focus on the task of creating multi-part assemblies : real-world objects made from a set of prefabricated parts joined by fixed connectors, such as LEGO ® builds. Multi-part assemblies must obey multiple constraints: all parts must be drawn from a preset library, parts must not collide or float, and the joined parts typically form a single connected component.
paragraphs.zh: 大语言模型（LLM）智能体在3D建模方面正变得越来越娴熟。 无需额外的微调，市售的智能体就能成功生成铰接物体 [ 58 , 45 ] 、场景 [ 52 ] 以及构造实体几何模型 [ 27 ] 。 然而，它们在构建面向物理世界的物体时仍然面临挑战。 我们专注于创建多部件组装的任务：即由一组通过固定连接件连接的预制部件构成的现实世界物体，例如乐高 ® 拼搭作品。 多部件组装必须遵守多种约束：所有部件必须取自预设的部件库，部件之间不得碰撞或悬空，且连接后的部件通常构成单个连通分量。

paragraphs.en: We argue that designing a toolkit for multi-part assembly creation is sufficient to enable agents to create physically valid builds. This toolkit should include (1) an assembly API , which provides an ergonomic programmatic interface for 3D creation; and (2) a validator , which provides feedback on a finished build’s physical validity. The need for a toolkit is independent of how powerful a coding agent is . We observe that GPT-6 Astra with Codex, when asked to make brick builds, already writes scripts to generate and validate its output more than 80% of the time ( Appendix D ). For complex physical domains, this self-validation is often not enough, resulting in builds that do not satisfy physical constraints, containing colliding, floating, or disconnected parts ( Fig. 2 ). Even if an agent is powerful enough to write a perfect toolkit, separately developing a toolkit remains important to reduce token usage and avoid repeated work. Existing toolkits for agentic 3D generation [ 58 , 45 ] are usually intended for digital asset creation; as they do not consider physical constraints, they cannot be repurposed as-is to create real-world objects.
paragraphs.zh: 我们认为，设计一个用于多部件组装创建的工具包，足以让智能体创建出物理上有效的作品。 该工具包应包含：（1）一个组装API，为3D创作提供符合人体工程学的程序化接口；（2）一个验证器，为完成的作品的物理有效性提供反馈。 对工具包的需求与编码智能体本身的强大程度无关。 我们观察到，GPT-6 Astra 搭配 Codex 在被要求制作积木作品时，已经有超过80%的情况下会自行编写脚本来生成并验证其输出（附录 D）。 对于复杂的物理领域，这种自我验证往往并不足够，导致生成的作品不满足物理约束，包含相互碰撞、悬浮或断开连接的部件（图 2）。 即使智能体强大到能够编写出一个完美的工具包，单独开发一个工具包仍然很重要，因为这可以减少 token 使用量并避免重复工作。 现有的面向智能体3D生成的工具包 [58, 45] 通常是为数字资产创作而设计的；由于它们不考虑物理约束，因此无法直接复用于创建现实世界中的物体。

paragraphs.en: We focus on the domain of LEGO ® generation as it is a commonly available yet complex system, consisting of thousands of parts that connect in dozens of ways. Our key insight is to merge agentic code-as-3D-models with the regularity of brick parts. Parts can be modeled as geometries with localized connectors that have programmatic rules for assembly (e.g., studs interlock with antistuds). From this perspective, we leverage the physical production rules for snap-fit brick builds [ 6 ] to create an ergonomic assembly API. Then, given an image or text prompt, our task is to generate a program using this API that, when compiled, produces a LEGO ® brick build in the standard LDraw format [ 21 ] . This build should include a list of library part placements, and it must be physically feasible , having no intersecting or floating parts and forming a connected structure if possible. While there are several specialized brick generation methods [ 50 , 10 , 11 , 19 , 37 , 48 , 36 , 53 ] , some of which consider physical constraints, they generally exhibit worse generalization and lower fidelity than commercial LLM agents on the same task. Hence, we wish to achieve this task agentically.
paragraphs.zh: 我们聚焦于 LEGO® 生成这一领域，因为它是一个常见可得却又复杂的系统，由数千个部件构成，这些部件以数十种方式相互连接。 我们的核心洞见是将智能体的代码即三维模型与积木部件的规则性相融合。 部件可以建模为带有局部连接器的几何体，这些连接器具有用于组装的程序化规则（例如，凸点与凹点相互咬合）。 从这一视角出发，我们利用卡扣式积木搭建的物理生产规则 [ 6 ] 来创建一个符合人体工程学的组装 API。 然后，给定一张图像或文本提示，我们的任务是生成一个使用该 API 的程序，该程序经编译后会以标准 LDraw 格式 [ 21 ] 生成一个 LEGO® 积木搭建作品。 该搭建作品应包含一个库部件放置位置的列表，并且必须是物理可行的，即不存在相交或悬空的部件，并在可能的情况下形成一个连通的结构。 虽然已有若干专门化的积木生成方法 [ 50 , 10 , 11 , 19 , 37 , 48 , 36 , 53 ] ，其中一些考虑了物理约束，但在同一任务上，它们通常表现出比商用大语言模型智能体更差的泛化能力和更低的保真度。 因此，我们希望以智能体方式完成这一任务。

paragraphs.en: Early work treats brick build generation as an optimization problem over a target shape. Legolization [ 34 ] voxelizes a 3D mesh, merges voxels into standard bricks, and iteratively re-merges regions identified as unstable. Subsequent work captures finer geometric detail through feature-aware shape approximation and non-rectangular bricks [ 57 , 59 ] , assembles bricks sequentially via Bayesian optimization [ 17 ] , or optimizes Technic assemblies to match annotated sketches [ 49 ] . Retrieval-based methods map images to figurines assembled from prebuilt templates [ 56 , 9 ] . These methods are limited by small brick vocabularies, explicit geometric guidance, or fixed templates.
paragraphs.zh: 早期工作将积木模型生成视为针对目标形状的优化问题。 Legolization [34] 将三维网格体素化，把体素合并为标准积木，并迭代地重新合并被识别为不稳定的区域。 后续工作通过特征感知的形状近似和非矩形积木捕捉更精细的几何细节 [57, 59]，通过贝叶斯优化按顺序装配积木 [17]，或优化 Technic 拼装结构以匹配标注的草图 [49]。 基于检索的方法将图像映射为由预构建模板拼装而成的人偶 [56, 9]。 这些方法受限于较小的积木词表、显式的几何引导或固定的模板。

paragraphs.en: Learning-based methods generate brick structures directly from data. These approaches adapt graph generative models [ 41 ] , predict voxel representations that are assembled into bricks algorithmically [ 24 , 4 ] , learn sequential construction policies [ 7 ] , or use diffusion to predict labeled voxels within a single category [ 10 ] . Autoregressive methods generate bricks conditioned on text or images. BrickGPT [ 37 ] fine-tunes an LLM to generate stable structures, but is restricted to eight rectangular brick types across 21 object categories. LEGO-Maker [ 11 ] generates builds from images, but supports only axis-aligned orientations and two categories. LegoACE [ 50 ] and BrickNet [ 19 ] scale to open-vocabulary generation by training on large collections of human-designed builds. However, LegoACE learns connectivity implicitly and can produce disconnected components, while BrickNet represents assemblies as connector graphs but accumulates collisions over longer build sequences. Brick-Composer [ 30 ] instead approaches assembly from target views as sequential brick selection and pose estimation, training a multimodal LLM on simulator-generated data and feedback. Other methods improve buildability through preference optimization or reinforcement learning [ 36 , 48 ] . In contrast, BrickWright utilizes pre-trained models to build arbitrary objects without task-specific training, verifies collisions and connectivity in a feedback loop, and supports articulation. Concurrent with our work, BrickBench [ 20 ] introduces a toolkit for agentic brick build creation, focusing on benchmarking the performance of different agents.

paragraphs.en: Representing shapes as programs provides structured descriptions of geometry and part relationships [ 39 , 42 , 16 ] . Separately, LLMs have been shown to reason more reliably when they write code and offload exact computation to an interpreter [ 8 ] . Building on both ideas, agents have been applied to modeling individual objects as code, typically through plan-execute-critique loops. Prior work augments this loop with API retrieval [ 32 ] , domain-specific languages [ 45 ] , or procedural part-based modeling [ 27 ] , with some supporting articulation [ 45 , 27 , 58 , 23 ] . In CAD, LLMs have been fine-tuned to generate parametric modeling code [ 47 , 12 , 18 ] , while tool-augmented agents generate and refine parts and assemblies [ 35 , 40 , 1 , 55 ] . Articraft [ 58 ] generates articulated assets using a custom SDK and a minimal harness that provides textual feedback from tools that probe the model code. Unlike these systems, where the agent generates geometry or infers inter-part relationships, BrickWright assembles fixed parts whose connectors determine how they attach and move.
paragraphs.zh: 将形状表示为程序可以为几何体与零件关系提供结构化的描述 [ 39 , 42 , 16 ] 。 另一方面，已有研究表明，大语言模型在编写代码并将精确计算交给解释器执行时，推理会更加可靠 [ 8 ] 。 结合这两种思想，智能体已被用于将单个物体建模为代码，通常采用「规划—执行—批判」的循环方式。 已有工作通过 API 检索 [ 32 ] 、领域专用语言 [ 45 ] 或基于零件的程序化建模 [ 27 ] 来增强这一循环，其中一些还支持关节连接 [ 45 , 27 , 58 , 23 ] 。 在 CAD 领域，大语言模型已被微调用于生成参数化建模代码 [ 47 , 12 , 18 ] ，而借助工具增强的智能体则可以生成并优化零件与装配体 [ 35 , 40 , 1 , 55 ] 。 Articraft [ 58 ] 使用自定义 SDK 和一个最小化框架来生成带关节的资产，该框架通过探测模型代码的工具提供文本反馈。 与这些由智能体生成几何体或推断零件间关系的系统不同，BrickWright 组装的是固定的零件，其连接件决定了零件的连接方式与运动方式。

paragraphs.en: To improve physical validity, prior work refines shapes or layouts after generation [ 5 , 51 , 54 , 29 , 25 ] , fine-tunes generators on simulator feedback [ 26 ] , or guides diffusion sampling with physical constraints [ 33 ] . Geometric analysis has also been used to plan LEGO assembly sequences without explicit connector information [ 2 ] . For brick structures, stability has been assessed through force-based equilibrium analysis [ 34 , 37 , 31 ] or physics simulation [ 17 , 46 ] . In contrast, BrickWright uses an executable verifier to check for collisions, floating parts, and connectivity, allowing a pre-trained agent to iteratively repair builds without task-specific training. Incorporating force-based stability analysis [ 34 , 31 ] is a natural extension.

paragraphs.en: Given a natural-language or image description, our task is to generate a physically feasible brick build from a fixed part catalog. A brick build is defined as an ordered sequence of placements . Each placement consists of an element or a nested brick build, together with a rigid transformation relative to the containing build. An element specifies a single part drawn from the catalog and a color. Elements expose typed connectors , such as studs, whose compatibility and relative alignment determine valid connections . A build is valid if it uses only catalog parts and contains no colliding (intersecting) or floating parts. It forms a connected component if one can draw a path of connections between any two elements in the build. We define a build to be physically feasible if it is valid and contains as few connected components as possible. More complex feasibility considerations, such as ensuring a build is stable and has an executable assembly sequence, are left to future work. Note that although having a single connected component is desirable as it makes a build less likely to break apart in the physical world, builds with multiple components are still necessary in some cases: for example, two separate vehicles in a car chase scene.
paragraphs.zh: 给定一段自然语言或图像描述，我们的任务是从固定的零件目录中生成一个物理上可行的积木作品。 一个积木作品被定义为放置（placement）的有序序列。 每个放置由一个元件（element）或一个嵌套的积木作品组成，并附带相对于其所属作品的刚体变换。 一个元件指定从目录中选取的单个零件及其颜色。 元件暴露出类型化的连接器（connector），例如凸点（stud），其兼容性与相对对齐决定了有效连接（connection）。 如果一个作品只使用目录中的零件，且不包含碰撞（相交）或悬空的零件，则该作品是有效的。 如果能在作品中任意两个元件之间画出一条由连接构成的路径，则该作品构成一个连通分量。 我们定义：如果一个作品是有效的，并且包含尽可能少的连通分量，那么它就是物理可行的。 更复杂的可行性考量，例如确保作品稳定并具有可执行的装配顺序，留待未来工作解决。 请注意，尽管只有一个连通分量是理想的，因为它使作品在物理世界中更不容易散架，但在某些情况下包含多个连通分量的作品仍是必要的：例如，汽车追逐场景中的两辆独立车辆。

paragraphs.en: We introduce BrickWright ( Fig. 3 ), a framework for generating physically feasible brick builds using LLM agents. Using a lightweight harness, BrickWright guides a single agent to write Python code that produces a brick build using a custom toolkit called BrickLayer . If the build passes a set of predefined and agent-written tests, it is accepted; otherwise, the agent makes edits informed by the test results, following the commonly used plan-execute-validate loop.

paragraphs.en: LDraw [ 21 ] , the standard text format for LEGO ® builds, includes no physical validation and is not very ergonomic : it only allows users to place parts and sub-models by their absolute 3D poses. This makes it difficult to mate parts by their connectors or place them relative to others, which can lead to wasted tokens and misplaced components. To provide agents with an ergonomic interface for creating and validating brick builds, we introduce BrickLayer ( ), a Python package that includes functions for part discovery, assembly, and validation. paragraphs.en: The central objects of BrickLayer are Element , representing a single colored part, and LegoBuild , representing a brick build. Both objects support a unified LegoGeometry interface; this interface exposes dimensions and available connectors, which can be filtered by type and position. We use BrickNet’s connector annotations [ 19 ] , which mark the local frames of the connectors on each part, along with compatible connector types and the joints they form: fixed, revolute, ball, prismatic, or cylindrical. For example, studs and antistuds join with a revolute joint. As BrickNet annotations do not differentiate between prismatic and cylindrical joints, we determine a sliding joint’s type by rotating it 15 ∘ 15^{\circ} about its axis in one direction; if a collision occurs, we mark the joint prismatic.
paragraphs.zh: BrickLayer 的核心对象是 Element（表示单个彩色零件）和 LegoBuild（表示一个积木搭建）。 两种对象都支持统一的 LegoGeometry 接口；该接口暴露尺寸和可用的连接器，可按类型和位置进行筛选。 我们使用 BrickNet 的连接器标注 [19]，该标注标记每个零件上连接器的局部坐标系，以及兼容的连接器类型和它们形成的关节：固定、旋转、球形、滑动或圆柱。 例如，凸点和反凸点以旋转关节连接。 由于 BrickNet 标注不区分滑动关节和圆柱关节，我们通过将滑动关节绕其轴沿一个方向旋转 15 度来确定其类型；如果发生碰撞，我们将其标记为滑动关节。

paragraphs.en: A LegoBuild provides methods to list collisions, floating elements, and disconnected components. To determine whether two elements collide, we inset each mesh by 0.1 mm before checking for intersections, following BrickNet; snap connections between bricks are so tight that a naive mesh intersection check would report a false positive. The floater check first translates a build so its lowest point is at the ground plane. Then, it marks an element floating if it cannot reach a grounded element through mated connectors or supporting surface contacts . A surface contact is supporting if it has an upward component; lateral contact alone is insufficient. Two connectors form a connection if their local frames align, depending on their joint type; for example, a fixed joint requires the two frames to align exactly, while a revolute joint additionally admits a rotational degree of freedom. For builds with user-annotated articulations, a posed method allows an agent to create a snapshot of the build with joints set to specified articulation parameters, to validate physical feasibility under joint motion. Posing works with models whose kinematic structure forms a tree.
paragraphs.zh: LegoBuild 提供了列出碰撞、悬浮元素和不连通组件的方法。 为了判断两个元素是否碰撞，我们遵循 BrickNet 的做法，在检测相交前将每个网格内缩 0.1 毫米；积木之间的卡扣连接非常紧密，直接进行网格相交检测会产生误报。 悬浮检测首先平移整个作品，使其最低点位于地面平面上。 然后，如果某个元素无法通过已连接的连接器或支撑性表面接触到达任何接地元素，则将其标记为悬浮。 只有具有向上分量的表面接触才算支撑性接触；仅有侧向接触是不够的。 两个连接器的局部坐标系根据其关节类型对齐时即构成一个连接；例如，固定关节要求两个坐标系完全对齐，而旋转关节还允许一个旋转自由度。 对于带有用户标注关节的作品，系统提供摆位方法，允许智能体将关节设置为指定的关节参数并创建作品快照，以验证关节运动下的物理可行性。 摆位功能适用于运动学结构为树状的模型。

paragraphs.en: BrickWright is a framework for agentic brick build creation using BrickLayer. It provides a single agent with a set of tools and prompts it to create a build by writing and revising a single Python file in a plan-execute-validate loop, inspired by Articraft [ 58 ] . The BrickWright environment exposes the tools validate , which runs agent-written tests alongside fixed collision and floating checks; render , which renders the build into a multi-view sheet or from a single specified view; and finalize , which marks the build as finished.
paragraphs.zh: BrickWright 是一个基于 BrickLayer 的智能体式积木搭建创作框架。 它为单个智能体提供一组工具，并提示其通过编写和修改单个 Python 文件来创建搭建作品，采用「规划-执行-验证」循环，灵感来自 Articraft [ 58 ]。 BrickWright 环境提供了以下工具：validate，运行智能体编写的测试以及固定的碰撞与悬空检查；render，将搭建作品渲染成多视图图版或从指定的单一视角渲染；finalize，将搭建作品标记为已完成。

sents.en: BrickWright is a framework for agentic brick build creation using BrickLayer.
sents.zh: BrickWright 是一个基于 BrickLayer 的智能体式积木搭建创作框架。

sents.en: It provides a single agent with a set of tools and prompts it to create a build by writing and revising a single Python file in a plan-execute-validate loop, inspired by Articraft [ 58 ] .

sents.en: The BrickWright environment exposes the tools validate , which runs agent-written tests alongside fixed collision and floating checks; render , which renders the build into a multi-view sheet or from a single specified view; and finalize , which marks the build as finished.
sents.zh: BrickWright 环境提供了以下工具：validate，运行智能体编写的测试以及固定的碰撞与悬空检查；render，将搭建作品渲染成多视图图版或从指定的单一视角渲染；finalize，将搭建作品标记为已完成。

paragraphs.en: In its system prompt, BrickWright instructs an agent to make a short internal plan, then write a Python file, build.py , containing two functions: create_build() , which returns a LegoBuild , and run_tests() , which runs a set of agent-written tests against the completed build. After creating build.py , the agent is instructed to iteratively call validate and edit the build file until all tests pass, then call render ; if it judges the render satisfactory, it should then call finalize ; otherwise, it should revise build.py and repeat validation. Besides these instructions, BrickWright includes only the BrickLayer documentation in its system prompt, and the input text or image in a user prompt. It does not provide the agent with detailed planning advice, complete build examples, or building tips beyond the plan-execute-validate loop; the loop alone is sufficient for even lightweight agents to produce a feasible build.
paragraphs.zh: 在其系统提示词中，BrickWright 指示智能体先制定一个简短的内部计划，然后编写一个名为 build.py 的 Python 文件，其中包含两个函数：create_build()，返回一个 LegoBuild；以及 run_tests()，针对完成的拼搭作品运行一组由智能体编写的测试。 在创建 build.py 之后，智能体被指示迭代地调用 validate 并编辑拼搭文件，直到所有测试通过，然后调用 render；如果它认为渲染结果令人满意，则应调用 finalize；否则，它应修改 build.py 并重复验证过程。 除了这些指示之外，BrickWright 在其系统提示词中仅包含 BrickLayer 文档，并在用户提示词中提供输入的文本或图像。 它不会向智能体提供详细的规划建议、完整的拼搭示例，或超出「计划-执行-验证」循环之外的拼搭技巧；仅凭这个循环就足以让即使是轻量级的智能体也能生成可行的拼搭作品。

paragraphs.en: As Articraft is intended for primitive-based 3D generation, we minimally modify it to use a library of LDraw part meshes rather than mesh primitives. We adjust Articraft’s system prompt to reword phrases that do not work with brick builds, such as allowing geometry overlaps.

paragraphs.en: We report metrics on physical feasibility as defined in Sec. 3 ; prompt adherence as judged by VQAScore [ 28 ] , Perception Encoder [ 3 ] , and SigLIP 2 [ 43 ] ; average brick count per build; and average time and cost per prompt. Validity and connectivity are first evaluated using BrickLayer’s validator. Then, to independently verify the metrics’ accuracy, we flag potential false positives for review by a human experienced with LEGO ® design. Potential false positives include collisions resolved by a tested shift of at most 0.2 mm and disconnected components containing parts without connector annotations. Human review increases collision-free rates by 0.2 percentage points for BrickNet and Claude Code (Haiku), 1.4 for Codex (Sol), and 1.0 for Codex (Astra). It reduces mean component counts by 0.13 for Codex (Sol), 0.10 for Codex (Astra), and 0.12 for Articraft; changes for the remaining methods are below 0.02 components per build. Numbers in Tab. 1 are post-review.

paragraphs.en: Compared to vanilla agent baselines, builds produced by BrickWright-equipped agents exhibit greatly improved physical feasibility with broadly comparable token costs ( Tab. 1 ). Impressively, the lightweight model Luna, which has only a 9% baseline validity rate, achieves 100% validity when used with BrickWright. This increase in physical validity is not accompanied by a significant decrease in complexity or fidelity; on average, BrickWright agents use more bricks and more unique parts than vanilla agent baselines, while improving prompt adherence for lightweight models (Haiku, Luna) and maintaining it for powerful models (Sol, Astra). These gains hold even with BrickWright’s minimal harness, whereas Codex and Claude Code can read, write, and execute arbitrary files. BrickWright-equipped agents additionally outperform specially trained text-to-brick models in overall feasibility and prompt adherence. The Articraft baseline, which is intended for digital 3D assets, yields comparable prompt adherence but worse physical validity at more than twice the cost of BrickWright. The visual results in Fig. 6 show how BrickWright reduces physical artifacts for all agent backends and improves the coherence of builds created by lightweight agents. On average, most BrickWright agents use 2–3 validate calls; Luna uses 4–5 ( Tab. 1 ).
paragraphs.zh: 与原始智能体基线相比，配备 BrickWright 的智能体所构建的作品在物理可行性方面有大幅提升，同时 token 成本大体相当（表 1）。 令人印象深刻的是，轻量级模型 Luna 的基线有效率仅有 9%，而在与 BrickWright 配合使用时达到了 100% 的有效率。 物理有效性的提升并未伴随复杂度或保真度的显著下降；平均而言，BrickWright 智能体比原始智能体基线使用更多的积木块和更多种类的独特零件，同时提升了轻量级模型（Haiku、Luna）的提示遵循度，并保持了强大模型（Sol、Astra）的提示遵循度。 即使在 BrickWright 极简的框架下，这些收益依然成立，而 Codex 和 Claude Code 可以读取、写入并执行任意文件。 此外，配备 BrickWright 的智能体在整体可行性和提示遵循度方面均优于专门训练的文本转积木模型。 面向数字 3D 资产的 Articraft 基线在提示遵循度上与 BrickWright 相当，但物理有效性更差，且成本超过 BrickWright 的两倍。 图 6 的可视化结果展示了 BrickWright 如何为所有智能体后端减少物理瑕疵，并提升轻量级智能体所构建作品的连贯性。 平均而言，大多数 BrickWright 智能体使用 2–3 次 validate 调用；Luna 使用 4–5 次（表 1）。

paragraphs.en: We ablate BrickLayer’s two key components: the assembly API and the validator. In our first ablation, “w/o assembly API”, agents write a program that creates an LDraw file without using BrickLayer’s assembly functions. The LegoBuild abstraction is removed from BrickLayer, leaving only part search and physical validation, and its documentation is replaced by LDraw documentation of similar length. In our second ablation, “w/o validator”, agents are still told to make their output physically valid but cannot use the validate and render tools or BrickLayer’s physical validation functions. They are allowed to run their own validations using explore . We run ablations using Haiku, Luna, and Sol; we exclude Astra due to budget constraints.

paragraphs.en: BrickLayer’s assembly API greatly reduces token usage and makes it easier to create valid builds; when forced to work in LDraw rather than using LegoBuild , agents spend around twice the token cost and three times as many validate calls ( Tab. 1 ). Though stronger agents (Sol) still achieve 100% validity with no assembly API, weaker agents (Luna and Haiku) sometimes give up without finalizing the build, leading to validity scores below 100%. Without an assembly API, Luna’s prompt-similarity scores degrade significantly; it often produces simple structures ( Fig. 4 ) and its average part count drops from 27.4 to 7.2. Interestingly, merely using BrickLayer’s API without a provided validator boosts validity by up to 44 percentage points from Codex/Claude Code baselines! The automatic grid-snapping and connector-mating functions provided by BrickLayer help agents, especially lightweight ones, produce valid builds more easily. However, the validator remains a crucial component; without it, all agents score below 79% validity ( Tab. 1 ).

paragraphs.en: Frontier coding agents are capable of producing aesthetically pleasing LEGO ® brick builds from text or image prompts. However, even the most capable agents fail to produce physically feasible builds much of the time. Our framework, BrickWright, closes this gap by introducing a toolkit for brick build creation and validation. Equipped with BrickWright, even lightweight agents achieve 100% validity on 512 samples tested, while improving prompt adherence at a similar cost to agents without BrickWright. We hope this work highlights the importance of well-written construction APIs and physical validation in improving the performance of LLM agents on building tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 前沿编码智能体能够根据文本或图像提示生成美观的乐高®积木作品。 然而，即使是能力最强的智能体，也常常无法生成物理上可行的作品。 我们的框架 BrickWright 通过引入一套用于积木作品创建与验证的工具包，弥补了这一差距。 配备 BrickWright 后，即使是轻量级智能体，在测试的 512 个样本上也达到了 100% 的有效性，同时在成本与未配备 BrickWright 的智能体相近的情况下提升了对提示的遵循度。 我们希望这项工作能够凸显编写良好的构建 API 和物理验证在提升大语言模型智能体在搭建任务上表现方面的重要性。

paragraphs.en: Our definition of physical feasibility does not cover valid assembly sequences or stability analysis, which we leave to future work. Though agentic methods outperform specially trained models on brick build generation, they are generally slower and more costly. Effectively distilling the capabilities of powerful agents into smaller, faster models remains an interesting future direction.
paragraphs.zh: 我们对物理可行性的定义并未涵盖有效的装配序列或稳定性分析，我们将这些留待未来的工作。 尽管基于智能体的方法在积木搭建生成上优于专门训练的模型，但它们通常更慢、成本更高。 如何有效地将强大智能体的能力蒸馏到更小、更快的模型中，仍是一个有趣的未来研究方向。

paragraphs.en: Table 2 breaks down the reasons for failed validate calls. Physical checks account for most failures (63–85%), followed by runtime errors (11–28%) such as selecting a nonexistent connector or specifying an invalid part ID. For GPT agents, most physical failures are due to collisions, while Haiku’s main failure mode is connectivity. The more capable an agent, the more its physical failure distribution shifts toward collisions, away from floaters and connectivity.
paragraphs.zh: 表 2 对验证调用失败的原因进行了分类。 物理检查占失败的大多数（63–85%），其次是运行时错误（11–28%），例如选择了不存在的连接器或指定了无效的零件 ID。 对于 GPT 智能体，大多数物理失败源于碰撞，而 Haiku 的主要失败模式是连通性问题。 智能体能力越强，其物理失败的分布越向碰撞倾斜，而悬浮和连通性问题所占比例越少。

paragraphs.en: Car: “This is a red, open-top LEGO sports car featuring black racing stripes, yellow accents on the front and rear, and translucent orange headlights.” Boat: “This is a LEGO model of a small workboat or tugboat, featuring a red hull, an orange and white cabin with blue windows, a grey deck, and a black articulated crane on the stern.” Train: “This is a small, stylized LEGO model of a yellow and black steam locomotive, featuring a prominent smokestack, a curved boiler, a cab, and simple wheels, presented from multiple angles against a white background.” Snake: “This is a modular, dark green LEGO model of a snake or serpent, constructed from multiple articulated segments that allow it to be posed in various curved and straight configurations.” Squirrel: “This is a LEGO model of a black squirrel, constructed with dark grey and light grey bricks, featuring a large bushy tail, prominent white eyes, and holding two small, round objects in its paws.” Dragon: “This is a custom-built, orange LEGO model of a stylized, blocky creature resembling a dragon or dinosaur, featuring translucent flame elements at its rear and amber pieces for eyes.” Station: “This LEGO model is a white, multi-level medical or scientific station featuring an articulated lamp with a yellow lens, a control panel, and a cabinet with a yellow door.” Garden: “This LEGO model depicts a charming, rotating diorama of a small garden scene, featuring a pumpkin patch with a white fence on one side and a cylindrical well or shed with a ladder on the other, all built upon interconnected green baseplates.”
paragraphs.zh: 汽车：“这是一辆红色的乐高敞篷跑车，带有黑色赛车条纹，前后部有黄色点缀，以及半透明的橙色车灯。” 船：“这是一个小型工作艇或拖船的乐高模型，具有红色船体、带蓝色窗户的橙白相间船舱、灰色甲板，以及船尾的黑色铰接式起重机。” 火车：“这是一个黄黑相间蒸汽机车的乐高小型风格化模型，具有醒目的烟囱、弧形锅炉、驾驶室和简单车轮，以白色背景下的多角度呈现。” 蛇：“这是一个模块化的深绿色乐高蛇模型，由多个铰接段构成，可将其摆出各种弯曲和直线形态。” 松鼠：“这是一个黑色松鼠的乐高模型，采用深灰色和浅灰色积木构建，具有蓬松的大尾巴、醒目的白色眼睛，爪中握着两个小圆物体。” 龙：“这是一个橙色的乐高定制模型，是一个风格化的方块状生物，形似龙或恐龙，尾部有半透明火焰元素，眼睛使用琥珀色零件。” 车站：“这个乐高模型是一个白色多层医疗或科学站，配有带黄色灯罩的铰接灯、控制面板，以及一扇黄色门的柜子。” 花园：“这个乐高模型呈现了一个迷人的旋转微缩小花园场景，一侧是带白色栅栏的南瓜地，另一侧是带梯子的圆柱形水井或棚屋，全部建立在相互连接的绿色底板上。”

paragraphs.en: Piano: “This LEGO model is a compact, white grand piano with tan and black keys, featuring a hinged lid and built from various brick types including technic pieces.” Scene: “This LEGO model depicts a dilapidated, single-room shelter or bunker with crumbling brown and tan walls, containing a simple bed, a rifle, a sack, and a small cache of money.”
paragraphs.zh: 钢琴：“这个乐高模型是一个紧凑的白色三角钢琴，配有棕色和黑色的琴键，带有可开合的铰链琴盖，由包括科技件在内的各种积木类型搭建而成。”场景：“这个乐高模型描绘了一个破旧的单间庇护所或碉堡，拥有残破的棕色和棕褐色墙壁，里面有一张简易的床、一支步枪、一个麻袋和一小笔藏起来的钱。”

paragraphs.en: Image-conditioned generation: All three examples use the prompt “Match the image as closely as possible.” Ramen bar: “A cozy ramen bar interior with an open kitchen and diners.” Arctic observatory: “An Arctic observatory beneath the aurora.” Mountainside city: “A mountainside city in 15,000+ parts, with terraced houses, winding stairs, bridges, and waterfalls.” Build editing: Starting prompt —“A compact timber-framed cottage with a steep red roof.” Edit 1 —“Double the cottage’s depth; preserve its width, height, and timber-framed style.” Edit 2 —“Reshape its roof into a dark-blue gambrel, keeping the stretched walls and chimney.”
paragraphs.zh: 图像条件生成：三个示例均使用提示词「尽可能贴合图像」。拉面馆：「一个拥有开放式厨房和食客的温馨拉面馆内部」。北极观测站：「极光之下的北极观测站」。山腰城市：「一座由 15,000+ 个零件组成的山腰城市，带有梯田式房屋、蜿蜒的阶梯、桥梁和瀑布」。建筑编辑：初始提示词——「一座有着陡峭红屋顶的紧凑木框架小屋」。编辑 1——「将小屋的深度加倍；保持其宽度、高度和木框架风格」。编辑 2——「将其屋顶重塑为深蓝色复折式屋顶，保留拉伸后的墙体和烟囱」。

paragraphs.en: We give a short analysis of the brick build creation process of baseline GPT-6 Astra, used with Codex. We inspect the Python programs produced and executed by the agent during generation (whether inline or from a file) and classify them as generators and/or validators by using heuristics that trace the program’s abstract syntax tree (AST). If a program calls write_text() or write_bytes() on a model.ldr file or open s the file in a mode with write access, we classify it as a generator. If a program reads model.ldr and includes an assertion or error involving values derived from model.ldr , we classify it as a validator. Out of 512 builds created using prompts from BrickNet-512, 471 (92%) use a generator and 424 (83%) use a validator.
paragraphs.zh: 我们对基线 GPT-6 Astra（配合 Codex 使用）的积木搭建生成过程进行了简要分析。 我们检查智能体在生成过程中产生并执行的 Python 程序（无论是内联还是来自文件），并通过追踪程序抽象语法树（AST）的启发式方法，将其分类为生成器和/或验证器。 如果程序对 model.ldr 文件调用 write_text() 或 write_bytes()，或以具有写权限的模式打开该文件，我们将其分类为生成器。 如果程序读取 model.ldr，并包含涉及从 model.ldr 导出的值的断言或错误，我们将其分类为验证器。 在使用 BrickNet-512 提示词创建的 512 个搭建中，471 个（92%）使用了生成器，424 个（83%）使用了验证器。
